meta.note: The 'distance_and_connectivity' section is based on real, publicly verifiable geographic distances (web-searched and cross-checked across multiple sources). All other sections (bus routes, timing, fees, GPS tracking, driver contact, schedule changes, lost & found, vehicle policy) are generated for this academic project to be realistic and scale-consistent with a 50,000+ student university with a large day-scholar population. None of the generated sections should be treated as officially confirmed university policy.

data_types.generated_for_project: Realistic, scale-consistent data created for this academic project

bus_routes_covered.description: Given the university's large day-scholar population, university bus services cover multiple routes across Vadodara city and surrounding areas.
coverage_areas: Central Vadodara (Sayajigunj, Alkapuri, Race Course area)
Waghodia Road and surrounding localities (closer to campus)
Select outer routes toward nearby towns for students commuting from a wider catchment area
bus_routes_covered.note: Exact route numbers and stop lists are published each semester by the transport office based on demand and are subject to change.

bus_timing_per_shift.morning_pickup: Buses typically begin pickup from designated city stops between 6:30 AM and 8:00 AM, timed to arrive on campus before the 9:30 AM start of classes.
bus_timing_per_shift.evening_drop: Return buses typically depart from campus shortly after the 4:20 PM campus closing time, with drop-offs along the same routes in reverse order.
bus_timing_per_shift.additional_shifts: Additional late-evening shuttles may run for students attending extra classes, lab sessions, or club/event activities running past the standard campus hours.

bus_fee.structure: Bus fees are generally charged on an annual or semester basis, varying by route distance/zone.
bus_fee.approximate_range: Commonly in the range of ₹15,000 to ₹35,000 per year depending on the route/zone, payable along with or shortly after tuition fee payment.
bus_fee.note: Students may opt in/out of the bus service each year based on their residential situation (hosteler vs. day scholar commuting independently).

gps_tracking.availability: University buses are typically fitted with GPS tracking, allowing students and parents to track bus location in real time via a transport tracking app or the student ERP portal's transport module.
gps_tracking.benefit: Helps students time their arrival at pickup points and provides parents visibility into safe arrival/departure, particularly valued for day-scholar safety.

driver_conductor_contact_and_helpline.structure: Each bus route typically has an assigned driver and conductor, with the conductor's contact number shared with regular commuting students at the start of the term.
driver_conductor_contact_and_helpline.central_helpline: A central transport department helpline is generally available during operating hours for route queries, delays, or complaints, separate from individual driver/conductor numbers.

holiday_and_exam_period_schedule_changes.holiday_schedule: Bus services are suspended on university-declared holidays and reduced during long breaks (summer/winter vacation), with advance notice shared via the ERP portal/notice boards.
holiday_and_exam_period_schedule_changes.exam_period_adjustments: During exam periods, additional early-morning or midday shift buses may be added to accommodate variable exam timings, alongside the standard shift schedule.

lost_and_found_policy.process: Items lost on university buses can be reported to the transport department office or the respective route's driver/conductor; found items are typically logged and held at the transport office for a specified period (commonly 30 days) before being handed over to general campus lost-and-found or disposed of per policy.
lost_and_found_policy.reporting_window: Students are encouraged to report lost items as soon as possible, ideally on the same day, to maximize recovery chances.

private_vehicle_and_parking_policy.two_wheeler_and_car_policy: Students are permitted to bring personal two-wheelers/cars to campus, subject to registration with campus security and display of a valid parking permit/sticker.
private_vehicle_and_parking_policy.parking_zones: Designated parking zones are allocated separately for two-wheelers and four-wheelers, typically located near academic blocks and hostel entrances, with security patrol coverage.
private_vehicle_and_parking_policy.restrictions: Parking outside designated zones, or in fire-access/emergency lanes, is prohibited and subject to a fine or vehicle clamping in repeated violation cases.
private_vehicle_and_parking_policy.helmet_and_safety_rules: Two-wheeler riders are expected to comply with standard traffic safety norms (helmet usage) while riding within campus premises.

distance_and_connectivity.nearest_airport: Vadodara Airport (BDQ) is approximately 18-20 km from the campus, roughly a 30-40 minute drive; it connects to major cities including Mumbai, Delhi, and Bengaluru.
distance_and_connectivity.nearest_railway_station: Vadodara Junction Railway Station is approximately 15-20 km from the campus, roughly a 25-30 minute drive; it is a major rail junction on the Mumbai-Delhi line.
distance_and_connectivity.nearest_bus_stand: The Vadodara Central Bus Stand (CBS) is approximately 18 km from the campus, roughly a 20-minute drive by local bus, taxi, or auto-rickshaw.
distance_and_connectivity.onward_local_travel: From any of these three points, students can reach campus via local bus, auto-rickshaw, or app-based cab (Ola/Uber); approximate taxi fares from the airport/railway station range from ₹300-₹500.

local_auto_and_cab_availability.availability: Auto-rickshaws are readily available near campus and throughout Vadodara city; app-based cab services (Ola/Uber) are also commonly used and generally reliable for reaching/leaving campus.
local_auto_and_cab_availability.note: Shared auto-rickshaws are a common, budget-friendly option for short-distance travel between campus and nearby localities.
